newsitem.title: USA: NYS Thruway unveils six-year, $1.55 billion plan.
newsitem.headline: NYS Thruway unveils six-year, $1.55 billion plan.

text.p: The New York State Thruway Authority on Monday unveiled a $1.55 billion capital plan for the next six years, which includes a $296 million construction program for 1997, one of the biggest in its history.
About 40 percent of this year's program will be paid for with bonds, with the remaining 60 percent financed from pay-as you-go revenues, the authority said.

In prepared remarks, Thruway Chairman Howard Steinberg added: "As a result of an improving economy and an aggressive effort to control costs, there will be no toll increase for Thruway customers in the foreseeable future."
More than 85 percent of the new program will be spent on roads, bridges and related facilities, with the rest going towards canals and required economic development projects.

Some of the larger items include $823 million for rehabilitating 323 bridges, including $137 million for the Tappan Zee, which carries more than 120,000 vehicles a day; $301 million for repairing 1,200 lane miles of highway, and $218 million for repairing or replacing heavy equipment and finishing electronic toll collection programs.
Another $166 million will be spent on the Canal System's infrastructure, with $47 million on mandated economic development projects.

"The Thruway boasts a fatality rate that is half the national average, and this long-term program of rehabilitation will help us sustain this standard," the chairman said, adding around $292 million will be spent in central New York.
